name: Fictional private payroll
description: Authored progressive withholding on actually received private income, using a representative resident within each cohort and 365-day annualisation relative to opening GDP per resident. The existing income-tax policy sets a standard marginal reference rate; source-defined bands scale it. Public/local wages and welfare are outside this private-income base. Collection capacity affects actual withholding; potential tax is not treasury cash or an arrears claim. No historical tax filing law, intra-cohort distribution or other tax bases are claimed. Fiscal AI reviews use the national daily balance after protected local claims, while earlier rules retain their original consolidated trigger. Authority, available cash, fees, review and real programme delivery remain ordinary shared constraints. This is an authored bounded heuristic, not historical government behavior or optimal economic planning. Newly disbursed loans have an authored 180-day bullet maturity. Opening debt remains a perpetual calibration, not a historical issuance. Scheduled principal uses available national cash after protected local claims and reservations, before interest and national purchases. Unpaid matured principal remains outstanding without being duplicated as operating arrears. Separate ordinary borrowing can fund repayment but is not guaranteed refinancing. No historical maturity curve, default/restructuring, FX or market pricing is claimed. Temporary cash retention protects only actual national cash after capital/local reservations, up to 1% opening GDP for at most 90 days. Approval falls by three points; a 90-day reuse cooldown applies from creation. Release, expiry or government change ends protection without cancelling any obligation or granting spending authority. Debt interest accrues at fixed 4% actual/365 on outstanding principal after scheduled principal settlement. Fractions carry without compounding; only whole reporting units become due. Cash payments and unpaid whole-unit external arrears reconcile separately. A sub-unit remainder survives retirement of principal and is not cash or spending authority. Taxes, wages, purchases and prices still use whole million-credit units. Grid programme commissioning is unavailable before 2000-01-31 in this fictional scenario. Agronomic planning is already eligible. Eligibility permits an ordinary proposal; it grants no research, adopted technology, cash, capacity or shortened construction. All prerequisites, governing backing, full funding and delivery remain necessary. Full research and adoption dynamics remain outside this scenario. Fictional legal sovereignty, occupation, civil administration, disputed claims and directional recognition are independently attributed bookmark references. Future records select later bookmarks, never force a campaign transfer. Unknown records are explicit; absent recognition means unknown. No military, diplomatic, revenue, border or map-geometry effects are granted. Economic preferences use explicit fiscal target ranges and importance weights, independently of ideology labels. Operating policy distance can lower the backing target for a governing coalition or ruling-party leadership, with gradual existing political reviews. Unknown positions create no pressure and remain identified. Aurora uses parliamentary coalition seats; Boreal begins under party-council leadership; Coral's royal route has advisory positions only. Positions grant no cash, votes, consent exemption or extra powers. Other preference dimensions and party organization remain unfinished. National food and energy reserves start empty. Ordinary consent and paid administration authorize fixed quoted-price import contracts, with full purchase cash reserved. Gradual procurement uses only import capacity remaining after civilian physical needs; no goods are created by proposal or consent. Stored goods cover post-import physical shortfalls automatically, while household affordability still applies. Food stocks spoil at the market storage rate; expiry or cancellation releases only unspent purchase reservations. Energy units are generic model equivalents, not a claim about electrical storage or fuel technologies. Events have stable country-scoped references across filtering, retention and save/load. Only a government's own retained events are available through reference lookup. An expired reference is not reused. Event reference exhaustion rejects a command or rolls back the incomplete daily step; previously completed days remain. Every earlier rules pack is preserved with its original definitions and behavior. Private policy lifecycle events carry an owned programme ID and recorded stage. The link is independent of translated text, row position or policy names and survives filtering, retention and save/load. It grants no foreign access, cash, consent exemption or operating effects. Earlier definitions and campaigns retain their exact bytes and rules. The authored 100-seat election rule allocates remaining seats across opposition parties in ascending stable party-ID order. The largest opposition party leads a successor coalition; equal seat totals choose the lowest stable party ID. Display names and input row order do not settle these choices. Older rules retain their original ordering. This is a reproducible game abstraction, not a claim about national electoral laws. Aurora has three authored parties with opening seats 60/20/20; the third party has explicitly unknown fiscal positions. Older review observations are retained as calendar-year sample summaries after leaving the 120-review recent window. This changes statistical retention only; it grants no resources or authority. All earlier rules packs keep their original behavior. Authored statutory prototype: higher new service programmes require a paid, consented and implemented legal authority. This is an original scenario rule, not a historical statement of national legislation. Stable live holder references and separately identified simulated successor bodies. Opening people and offices remain source references; future source terms do not force campaign outcomes. Authored stable identities for modeled governing routes and submission context. These are gameplay institutions, without claims about historical names, membership, founding dates or votes. Optional authored demographic exercise: every country uses the same coarse birth, mortality, age-split, family-formation and statistical-capacity assumptions. These are not historical national vital statistics, census quality rankings or migration estimates. Aggregate household units create no dwellings or wealth. Working age is not employment. Production and import capacity remain tied to opening physical need; new residents increase civilian demand without creating capacity. GDP remains an opening calibration. Migration moves residents between country/cohort stocks, without transferring pooled group cash, assets or arrears. Pooled claims and already-funded local financial obligations remain payable even if a cohort becomes empty; those transfers do not certify staffing or actual service delivery. Regional placement, housing constraints, individual labor mobility, inheritance and endogenous fertility remain unfinished. Authored cross-sectional joint membership profiles, not historical national prevalence, individual identity histories or records about real residents. Disjoint age/employment scopes prevent double-counting people. The employment membership reproduces existing modeled jobs; membership grants no cash, votes, powers or programme exemptions. Joint shares are explicitly configured, without assuming independent memberships. Parent/carer membership uses the model's 15+ bands, not a claim about legal adulthood. Union membership in this exercise is limited to modeled employed residents; retiree/other union membership and longitudinal joining/leaving remain unfinished. These common assumptions are shared across countries and economic cohorts. Authored auxiliary infrastructure network, not historical national sector output, deposits, asset holdings or productivity observations. Agriculture supplies industrial biomass; extraction supplies finite-deposit feedstocks and industrial fuel; manufacturing supplies tools and materials; construction supplies storable prefabricated assembly packages, not stored worker-hours; services supply nonstorable contracted inputs. These goods are distinct from national civilian Food/Energy. Paid programmes consume packages and funded public/maintenance services require actual inputs. A bounded share of live employed workers is reserved for this network and limited by actual private income paid; remaining workers belong to the older abstract civilian economy. Common stock targets, recipes, productivity and opening maintained-equipment readiness are scenario assumptions. Broader labor, private investment and product markets remain unfinished. Authored public auxiliary equipment investment, not historical industry ownership, national capital stocks or returns. Each paid programme commissions one country-specific build step after ordinary authority, consent, preparation, construction and actual assembly packages. Added batches and matching capital become available the following day and depend on previously settled physical maintenance readiness. Each installed level owes 10 basis points of opening annual GDP per 365 days in maintenance cash, with exact fractional carry, and needs one country maintenance unit per day. There are at most three additions per sector. These common calibrations do not create jobs, wages or GDP; private investment, profitability, depreciation and closures remain unfinished. Authored public auxiliary equipment retirement, not historical closures, private profitability or salvage values. A paid 20 basis point opening-GDP programme, with at least 30 days preparation and ordinary consent, retires one previously commissioned addition. Capacity and new maintenance obligations fall from the following day. Opening equipment cannot be retired. Sunk investment costs, existing arrears and fractional creditor claims remain; there are no cash proceeds or returned construction packages. Three additions per sector may operate simultaneously; retired additions may be replaced through ordinary paid investment. These common calibrations are gameplay assumptions, not national engineering estimates. Private firms, profits, depreciation and insolvency remain unfinished. Authored public auxiliary-inventory import and export contracts, not historical national trade volumes or private firm profits. Prices quote basis points of opening annual GDP per ten country-specific production lots. Ask prices exceed bids. Import contracts reserve their full quoted cash; all orders pay a nonrefundable one-basis-point administration fee. Ordinary authority and consent precede at most 30 daily fills. Imports arrive after production and before storage, and can support later construction delivery. Exports protect current domestic service use and packages needed by funded construction due that day. External supply and demand have separate per-good daily limits; exports also require actual counterparty cash. No bank credit, cash, wages or GDP is created. Purchase payments round up and sale receipts down on cumulative delivered quantities. Small interim fills can round to zero whole credits. Imported stocks remain subject to the same storage losses. Cancellation retains sunk administration, goods already delivered and payments already settled. Closed contracts remain in campaign history; only simultaneous open orders are limited. Export receipts are recorded separately from recurring tax revenue and are not forecast as guaranteed income. Bilateral trade, private ownership and profit-led firms remain unfinished. Authored household-owned aggregate civilian business cash exercise, not historical ownership or national profit accounts. Each existing Firms account represents one enterprise cohort; existing public industrial stocks and equipment remain public. Household groups own fixed shares in proportion to their authored opening savings weights, without individual ownership records. Every 30 elapsed campaign days, businesses autonomously distribute up to 25% of positive undistributed operating cash, while protecting actual trailing 30-day business payments. Household and external receipts add to earned cash; all business payments, including past distributions, subtract. Opening capital and every Treasury receipt are excluded. A missing owning population cohort suspends payouts without reallocating ownership. Payments enter household income before ordinary withholding. This transfers existing cash and creates no GDP, jobs, wages or new money. The government cannot order a private payout. Cash generation is not accrual profit; commodity cost valuation, public/mixed/cooperative ownership, conversions, insolvency and investment remain unfinished. Authored batch household settlement, not historical retail transactions. Desired basket spending, cash-limited planned budget, affordable food demand and physically delivered food remain distinct. The food part of the essential basket uses the actual settled food price and configured food budget share; spending above the essential basket is abstract other consumption. Households retain the quoted food budget corresponding to missing deliveries. Only delivered food is charged, rounded down within whole million-credit reporting units; the rounding discount is less than one reporting unit per group/day. The other basket component remains abstract, without an additional physical product market. Plans clear once per day in a single batch; retained cash is available for later days, without a same-day second auction or borrowing. Actual payments transfer existing household cash to businesses and enter ordinary business cash reconciliation. No cash, food, wages, jobs or GDP is created. Public industrial assets, private ownership weights and ordinary government authority remain unchanged. Accrual profit and production-cost valuation remain unfinished. Authored aggregate civilian business cost accounts, not historical firm financial statements. Actual private household factor payments are allocated 35% to domestic food production and 15% to domestic energy production; these direct cost shares round down, with remaining payments and idle production allocations expensed today. All preexisting factor payments remain actual transfers, not added payroll or employment. Moving weighted-average carrying costs pool opening stock cost, actual domestic factor costs and actual import payments. Closing stock value rounds down; removed cost is split between delivered use and spoilage, with the remainder charged to spoilage. An import payment delivering no whole quantity is expensed rather than capitalized. Opening civilian stocks are zero; public reserve releases have zero business acquisition cost and remain identified as public in-kind supplies. Energy use is a common period production expense; it is not added again to food inventory. Public auxiliary industrial stocks and equipment are excluded from private inventories and assets. Government policy contracts earn the standard 10% administration component at proposal, including immediate-consent routes; paid capital is deferred until actual delivery or recognized separately as retained termination income upon funded withdrawal. Amendment fees are earned administrative receipts. Existing unpaid maintenance claims are receivables, not repeated sales when collected. The modeled business result, including separately identified retained termination income, reconciles exactly to cash change, owner distributions, stock carrying costs, receivables and deferred contract receipts. Owner distributions are equity payments, never operating expenses. No cash, goods, wages, jobs, GDP or ownership conversion is created by valuation. Private fixed-asset depreciation, contractual unpaid payroll, corporate tax, firm investment and insolvency remain unfinished; the corporate cash distribution rule is preserved and does not pretend this cost account is a complete solvency or payout policy. Authored corporate payout policy, not historical financial statements or a complete insolvency model. This version supersedes the inherited operating-cash distribution base: every 30 elapsed days, businesses distribute at most the configured 25% of positive retained modeled earnings from the previous complete day. Retained earnings are cumulative modeled result less prior owner distributions; opening capital is excluded. Cash must additionally cover both actual trailing 30-day payments and all currently undelivered paid policy-contract capital. Only remaining cash can fund dividends; absent owning cohorts retain their ownership and block payouts. Payments enter ordinary household income and withholding. No money, goods, jobs, wages, GDP or public assets are created or converted. The payment buffer is a corporate liquidity policy, not a contractual debt or formal insolvency finding. Private investment, contractual unpaid payroll, private fixed assets, depreciation, corporate tax and insolvency remain unfinished. Authored private equipment market and corporate investment heuristic, not historical firm accounts. Opening private equipment is explicitly zero; opening civilian ownership remains unspecified and public assets are not converted. An external equipment supplier can deliver at most one equipment lot per country at each 30-day review, separate from public auxiliary-stock import quotas and public inventories. Firms pay the full 0.5% opening annual GDP price in cash. A delivered lot installs for 30 days, then contributes five opening-basis capacity points to food or energy for 3650 days. A good can have at most four unexpired lots including installation. Incremental output uses already paid civilian factors, with readiness derived from the last completed production-cost receipt against 1% of opening daily GDP; storage, shocks and the existing physical market settlement still constrain actual production. Straight-line whole-credit depreciation accumulates from commissioning to full cost at retirement; capital outlays are assets rather than factor expenses and net assets reconcile the cash-to-result bridge. At review firms prefer the greatest observed last-day avoidable import expense, with food winning exact ties. The quoted equipment price must be recovered within 730 days at that conditional saving, covered by prior-day retained earnings after actual dividends and current cash after both trailing 30-day payments and unfinished client advances. This is a conditional import-substitution heuristic, not guaranteed sales or a government order. Equipment creates no cash, residents, jobs, wages or GDP. A maximum of 256 retained acquisition receipts bounds history. Corporate taxation, contractual unpaid payroll, private finance, mergers and formal insolvency remain unfinished. Authored aggregate private employment contracts, not historical labor-force or salary data. Private contracts initially cover 70% of working-age residents in each non-public cohort, and 20% in the public cohort. Another 60% of the public cohort are possible public positions, estimated from actual service funding; these are not a second private payroll. Private positions are bounded by opening contract counts and current working-age residents. 70% of the existing opening private-factor income benchmark becomes a fixed aggregate wage bill, apportioned using existing income weights, then scaled to current contracted positions. Aggregate wage benchmarks and job-scaled daily bills round down to whole credit millions; largest remainders preserve each apportioned cash total exactly. The remaining 30% is non-wage factor income, still conditional on actual output and cash. Wage claims accrue before payment; actual available cash settles eligible cohort claims proportionally, with older claims first inside each cohort. Unpaid claims persist without creating spendable cash. Payments enter ordinary household income and withholding. Unpaid labor is expensed as period cost; later arrears payments do not fund current production or enter current inventory allocation. Payroll liabilities reduce business net earnings and the cash bridge, and protect cash from dividends and equipment purchases. Recruitment, dismissals, wage bargaining, individual contracts, private credit and formal insolvency remain unfinished. No residents, goods, cash or GDP are created by recording a contract or unpaid claim.

Withholding uses actual private income, representative cohort means and collection capacity; benefits and public/local wages remain outside this base. Full tax filing law and other bases are not modeled.

definitions.name: High-service appropriation authority
definitions.description: New service programmes at 14% of opening GDP or higher need this enacted permission. Existing operating services are retained. Enactment grants no services, cash or physical capacity; programme funding and implementation are separate.

demographics.description: Optional authored demographic exercise: every country uses the same coarse birth, mortality, age-split, family-formation and statistical-capacity assumptions. These are not historical national vital statistics, census quality rankings or migration estimates. Aggregate household units create no dwellings or wealth. Working age is not employment. Production and import capacity remain tied to opening physical need; new residents increase civilian demand without creating capacity. GDP remains an opening calibration. Migration moves residents between country/cohort stocks, without transferring pooled group cash, assets or arrears. Pooled claims and already-funded local financial obligations remain payable even if a cohort becomes empty; those transfers do not certify staffing or actual service delivery. Regional placement, housing constraints, individual labor mobility, inheritance and endogenous fertility remain unfinished.

social_memberships.description: Authored cross-sectional joint membership profiles, not historical national prevalence, individual identity histories or records about real residents. Disjoint age/employment scopes prevent double-counting people. The employment membership reproduces existing modeled jobs; membership grants no cash, votes, powers or programme exemptions. Joint shares are explicitly configured, without assuming independent memberships. Parent/carer membership uses the model's 15+ bands, not a claim about legal adulthood. Union membership in this exercise is limited to modeled employed residents; retiree/other union membership and longitudinal joining/leaving remain unfinished. These common assumptions are shared across countries and economic cohorts.

employment.name: Employed residents
employment.description: All residents holding a modeled job, exactly matching existing paid employment. This grants no additional income or votes.

parents.name: Parents and carers (15+ model)
parents.description: An authored parent/carer overlay in the model's 15+ bands, without claims about legal adulthood, individual relationships or national prevalence.

union.name: Union members
union.description: An authored overlay among modeled employed residents. It grants no organisation powers, legal recognition, votes or programme exemptions.

faith.name: Faith community members
faith.description: An authored nonexclusive overlay across age bands, without claims about one unified religious organisation or historical national prevalence.

production.description: Authored auxiliary infrastructure network, not historical national sector output, deposits, asset holdings or productivity observations. Agriculture supplies industrial biomass; extraction supplies finite-deposit feedstocks and industrial fuel; manufacturing supplies tools and materials; construction supplies storable prefabricated assembly packages, not stored worker-hours; services supply nonstorable contracted inputs. These goods are distinct from national civilian Food/Energy. Paid programmes consume packages and funded public/maintenance services require actual inputs. A bounded share of live employed workers is reserved for this network and limited by actual private income paid; remaining workers belong to the older abstract civilian economy. Common stock targets, recipes, productivity and opening maintained-equipment readiness are scenario assumptions. Broader labor, private investment and product markets remain unfinished.

industry.description: Authored public auxiliary equipment investment, not historical industry ownership, national capital stocks or returns. Each paid programme commissions one country-specific build step after ordinary authority, consent, preparation, construction and actual assembly packages. Added batches and matching capital become available the following day and depend on previously settled physical maintenance readiness. Each installed level owes 10 basis points of opening annual GDP per 365 days in maintenance cash, with exact fractional carry, and needs one country maintenance unit per day. There are at most three additions per sector. These common calibrations do not create jobs, wages or GDP; private investment, profitability, depreciation and closures remain unfinished. Authored public auxiliary equipment retirement, not historical closures, private profitability or salvage values. A paid 20 basis point opening-GDP programme, with at least 30 days preparation and ordinary consent, retires one previously commissioned addition. Capacity and new maintenance obligations fall from the following day. Opening equipment cannot be retired. Sunk investment costs, existing arrears and fractional creditor claims remain; there are no cash proceeds or returned construction packages. Three additions per sector may operate simultaneously; retired additions may be replaced through ordinary paid investment. These common calibrations are gameplay assumptions, not national engineering estimates. Private firms, profits, depreciation and insolvency remain unfinished.

retirement.description: Authored public auxiliary equipment retirement, not historical closures, private profitability or salvage values. A paid 20 basis point opening-GDP programme, with at least 30 days preparation and ordinary consent, retires one previously commissioned addition. Capacity and new maintenance obligations fall from the following day. Opening equipment cannot be retired. Sunk investment costs, existing arrears and fractional creditor claims remain; there are no cash proceeds or returned construction packages. Three additions per sector may operate simultaneously; retired additions may be replaced through ordinary paid investment. These common calibrations are gameplay assumptions, not national engineering estimates. Private firms, profits, depreciation and insolvency remain unfinished.

industrial_trade.description: Authored public auxiliary-inventory import and export contracts, not historical national trade volumes or private firm profits. Prices quote basis points of opening annual GDP per ten country-specific production lots. Ask prices exceed bids. Import contracts reserve their full quoted cash; all orders pay a nonrefundable one-basis-point administration fee. Ordinary authority and consent precede at most 30 daily fills. Imports arrive after production and before storage, and can support later construction delivery. Exports protect current domestic service use and packages needed by funded construction due that day. External supply and demand have separate per-good daily limits; exports also require actual counterparty cash. No bank credit, cash, wages or GDP is created. Purchase payments round up and sale receipts down on cumulative delivered quantities. Small interim fills can round to zero whole credits. Imported stocks remain subject to the same storage losses. Cancellation retains sunk administration, goods already delivered and payments already settled. Closed contracts remain in campaign history; only simultaneous open orders are limited. Export receipts are recorded separately from recurring tax revenue and are not forecast as guaranteed income. Bilateral trade, private ownership and profit-led firms remain unfinished.

businesses.description: Authored household-owned aggregate civilian business cash exercise, not historical ownership or national profit accounts. Each existing Firms account represents one enterprise cohort; existing public industrial stocks and equipment remain public. Household groups own fixed shares in proportion to their authored opening savings weights, without individual ownership records. Every 30 elapsed campaign days, businesses autonomously distribute up to 25% of positive undistributed operating cash, while protecting actual trailing 30-day business payments. Household and external receipts add to earned cash; all business payments, including past distributions, subtract. Opening capital and every Treasury receipt are excluded. A missing owning population cohort suspends payouts without reallocating ownership. Payments enter household income before ordinary withholding. This transfers existing cash and creates no GDP, jobs, wages or new money. The government cannot order a private payout. Cash generation is not accrual profit; commodity cost valuation, public/mixed/cooperative ownership, conversions, insolvency and investment remain unfinished.

consumption.description: Authored batch household settlement, not historical retail transactions. Desired basket spending, cash-limited planned budget, affordable food demand and physically delivered food remain distinct. The food part of the essential basket uses the actual settled food price and configured food budget share; spending above the essential basket is abstract other consumption. Households retain the quoted food budget corresponding to missing deliveries. Only delivered food is charged, rounded down within whole million-credit reporting units; the rounding discount is less than one reporting unit per group/day. The other basket component remains abstract, without an additional physical product market. Plans clear once per day in a single batch; retained cash is available for later days, without a same-day second auction or borrowing. Actual payments transfer existing household cash to businesses and enter ordinary business cash reconciliation. No cash, food, wages, jobs or GDP is created. Public industrial assets, private ownership weights and ordinary government authority remain unchanged. Accrual profit and production-cost valuation remain unfinished.

business_costs.description: Authored aggregate civilian business cost accounts, not historical firm financial statements. Actual private household factor payments are allocated 35% to domestic food production and 15% to domestic energy production; these direct cost shares round down, with remaining payments and idle production allocations expensed today. All preexisting factor payments remain actual transfers, not added payroll or employment. Moving weighted-average carrying costs pool opening stock cost, actual domestic factor costs and actual import payments. Closing stock value rounds down; removed cost is split between delivered use and spoilage, with the remainder charged to spoilage. An import payment delivering no whole quantity is expensed rather than capitalized. Opening civilian stocks are zero; public reserve releases have zero business acquisition cost and remain identified as public in-kind supplies. Energy use is a common period production expense; it is not added again to food inventory. Public auxiliary industrial stocks and equipment are excluded from private inventories and assets. Government policy contracts earn the standard 10% administration component at proposal, including immediate-consent routes; paid capital is deferred until actual delivery or recognized separately as retained termination income upon funded withdrawal. Amendment fees are earned administrative receipts. Existing unpaid maintenance claims are receivables, not repeated sales when collected. The modeled business result, including separately identified retained termination income, reconciles exactly to cash change, owner distributions, stock carrying costs, receivables and deferred contract receipts. Owner distributions are equity payments, never operating expenses. No cash, goods, wages, jobs, GDP or ownership conversion is created by valuation. Private fixed-asset depreciation, contractual unpaid payroll, corporate tax, firm investment and insolvency remain unfinished; the corporate cash distribution rule is preserved and does not pretend this cost account is a complete solvency or payout policy.

business_finance.description: Authored corporate payout policy, not historical financial statements or a complete insolvency model. This version supersedes the inherited operating-cash distribution base: every 30 elapsed days, businesses distribute at most the configured 25% of positive retained modeled earnings from the previous complete day. Retained earnings are cumulative modeled result less prior owner distributions; opening capital is excluded. Cash must additionally cover both actual trailing 30-day payments and all currently undelivered paid policy-contract capital. Only remaining cash can fund dividends; absent owning cohorts retain their ownership and block payouts. Payments enter ordinary household income and withholding. No money, goods, jobs, wages, GDP or public assets are created or converted. The payment buffer is a corporate liquidity policy, not a contractual debt or formal insolvency finding. Private investment, contractual unpaid payroll, private fixed assets, depreciation, corporate tax and insolvency remain unfinished.

private_investment.description: Authored private equipment market and corporate investment heuristic, not historical firm accounts. Opening private equipment is explicitly zero; opening civilian ownership remains unspecified and public assets are not converted. An external equipment supplier can deliver at most one equipment lot per country at each 30-day review, separate from public auxiliary-stock import quotas and public inventories. Firms pay the full 0.5% opening annual GDP price in cash. A delivered lot installs for 30 days, then contributes five opening-basis capacity points to food or energy for 3650 days. A good can have at most four unexpired lots including installation. Incremental output uses already paid civilian factors, with readiness derived from the last completed production-cost receipt against 1% of opening daily GDP; storage, shocks and the existing physical market settlement still constrain actual production. Straight-line whole-credit depreciation accumulates from commissioning to full cost at retirement; capital outlays are assets rather than factor expenses and net assets reconcile the cash-to-result bridge. At review firms prefer the greatest observed last-day avoidable import expense, with food winning exact ties. The quoted equipment price must be recovered within 730 days at that conditional saving, covered by prior-day retained earnings after actual dividends and current cash after both trailing 30-day payments and unfinished client advances. This is a conditional import-substitution heuristic, not guaranteed sales or a government order. Equipment creates no cash, residents, jobs, wages or GDP. A maximum of 256 retained acquisition receipts bounds history. Corporate taxation, contractual unpaid payroll, private finance, mergers and formal insolvency remain unfinished.

private_payroll.description: Authored aggregate private employment contracts, not historical labor-force or salary data. Private contracts initially cover 70% of working-age residents in each non-public cohort, and 20% in the public cohort. Another 60% of the public cohort are possible public positions, estimated from actual service funding; these are not a second private payroll. Private positions are bounded by opening contract counts and current working-age residents. 70% of the existing opening private-factor income benchmark becomes a fixed aggregate wage bill, apportioned using existing income weights, then scaled to current contracted positions. Aggregate wage benchmarks and job-scaled daily bills round down to whole credit millions; largest remainders preserve each apportioned cash total exactly. The remaining 30% is non-wage factor income, still conditional on actual output and cash. Wage claims accrue before payment; actual available cash settles eligible cohort claims proportionally, with older claims first inside each cohort. Unpaid claims persist without creating spendable cash. Payments enter ordinary household income and withholding. Unpaid labor is expensed as period cost; later arrears payments do not fund current production or enter current inventory allocation. Payroll liabilities reduce business net earnings and the cash bridge, and protect cash from dividends and equipment purchases. Recruitment, dismissals, wage bargaining, individual contracts, private credit and formal insolvency remain unfinished. No residents, goods, cash or GDP are created by recording a contract or unpaid claim.
